text:
ops-bot: PAGE: P99 latency SLO breach detected on cont-batch serving path (us-west2). alert_id=INC-2026-1773334444 :rotating_light:

sam: taking this. saw p95 ok but p99 jumping ~800ms -> 1.6s for streaming endpoints. streaming stalls and tail spikes. digging into batcher metrics now.

jess: fyi I'm on-call overlap til 18:30, will assist. any customer reports yet?

albert: quick snapshot from prometheus: cont_batch_queue_depth spiked, pack_shed_count up ~3500 in last 5m, kv_cache_evictions high. looks like mixed-seqlen wave causing big batches + KV churn.

maureen: @emma-cs any outbound customer alerts? i see a few support tickets showing UX timeouts on chat features.

emma-cs: reported from 6 customers (2 enterprise, 4 PLG). 3 customers reported streaming stalls where partial responses stop for ~1s then resume. they call it "chunking". logged as high priority.

sam: collecting traces for one request: trace id 0a1b2c - steps show long wait in batcher scheduling (wait_ms ~900) then quick model inference. implies scheduling/fairness preemption issue.

infra-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: canary rollout for batcher config change available. see https://console.redwood/investigations/1773334444

kevin: immediate mitigation options:
- reduce max_batch_size for cont-path pools to 8 (from 32)
- enable streaming preemptive-shed (allow long-streaming requests to preempt batched non-streaming)
- pin hot customers to dedicated pools (medium-term)

jess: recommend do the first two now. lower batch size should reduce tail buffer amplification. we can revert quickly if throughput SLO impacted.

sam: running quick config update on pool cont-rt-usw2-1: 
```bash
# lower max batch size
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood/internal/pools/cont-rt-usw2-1/config" -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN" -d '{"max_batch_size":8}'
```

albert: also toggling a fairness window tweak: reduce fairness_window_ms from 40 -> 20 to avoid long waits for short-seq requests.

infra-bot: applied config to cont-rt-usw2-1 (canary target: 2 nodes). rolling changes to remainder in 30s if metrics look good.

sam: initial metrics after canary (~60s): p99 dropped from 1.6s -> 780ms, p95 unchanged. stream stall reports still present but decreased. queue depth down ~45%. pack_shed_count down.

maureen: customer updates: sent interim note to enterprise customers that engineering is mitigating and we'll follow up with RCA.

emma-cs: customers acknowledged. one asked whether this is related to recent model upgrade -> clarified it's scheduling not model change.

kevin: followups to run if issue persists: enable kv-cache-stabilizer (slower eviction policy) and consider token-pacing config to avoid large batch formation from single long requests.

sam: interestingly, traces show a small set of very long sequences (L>1024) that accumulate with many short requests into same batches. mixed sequence lengths are amplifying latency. looks like packer is not differentiating by length on this pool.

albert: opened short-term patch to packer: prefer grouping by sequence-length-bin if that reduces padding amplification. patch ready to rollout as experiment.

jess: for safety let's not push packer patch infra-wide. keep to canary and observe. if p99 < 500ms we can expand.

infra-bot: canary expand started (20% nodes). will monitor 5m windows for p99, queue_depth, throughput.

sam: logs show a related symptom: KV cache thrash when big batches evict many context entries. enabling kv-cache-stabilizer on canary to reduce eviction rate. command: 
```bash
redwoodctl nodes update cont-rt-usw2-1 --kv-cache-stabilizer=on
```

albert: after kv-stabilizer + batch size drop + fairness tweak the canary p99 is ~420ms, streaming stalls almost gone (2 reports vs 12). pack_shed_count ~90% down.

maureen: good signal. customers want ETA for full fix and RCA.

kevin: post-incident action items (PIA):
- short: propagate config (max_batch_size=8, fairness_window_ms=20, kv-cache-stabilizer=on) to all cont-path pools in region within next 30m.
- medium: implement sequence-length-aware packer and token-pacing, rollout as controlled experiment.
- long: per-tenant QoS and ability to pin heavy seq customers to dedicated pools.

jess: i'll run the propagation playbook now. calling out checks.

sam: propagation started. using rolling update with health checks: require p99 < 700ms and error_rate increase <0.5%.

infra-bot: propagation progress: 40% -> 70% -> 100%. all nodes updated.

sam: post-propagation metrics (5m window): p99 stabilized ~390ms, p95 ~85ms, overall throughput within 3% of baseline. no significant error increase. streaming stall tickets down to 1 active.

emma-cs: pushing status update to customers now with ETA for RCA.

maureen: capture timeline for incident timeline. also note that the model upgrade question should be addressed in RCA (it wasn't the cause).

albert: created temp dashboard and saved trace set for later analysis: https://dash.redwood/internal/d/cont-batch-1773334444

kevin: write-up skeleton for RCA in PRD channels: root cause = scheduling amplification from mixed sequence lengths + KV cache eviction feedback loop; immediate mitigation = lower batching and fairness tweak + kv stabilizer; permanent fixes = seq-aware packing, token pacing, per-tenant QoS.

jess: handing off to next on-call @kevin. please monitor overnight for recurrence and follow PIA items.

kevin: ack. I'll own the postmortem and follow-ups. leaving note in #postmortems and will schedule runbook updates.

ops-bot: NOTE: incident INC-2026-1773334444 assigned to kevin. status=resolved -> monitoring. :white_check_mark:

sam: thanks all. next steps: pair with albert on packer experiment tomorrow, coordinate cs communications with maureen/emma.

kevin: closing thread for now, will reopen if signal reappears.
